questions.q: How did cholera bacteria adapt to humans in Bangladesh?
a: They formed tails and colonized the gut as a film
They entered through the skin and stayed dormant
They spread only through the air
They lived in rice and were eaten
questions.why: Lesson 1 says cholera bacteria formed tails and colonized the gut after people bathed in contaminated water.

questions.q: How did SARS reach five continents in one day?
a: Infected travelers carried it on flights
Migrating birds spread it across the globe
Contaminated food was shipped abroad
The virus traveled through ocean currents
questions.why: Lesson 2 traces SARS through a doctor, a flight attendant and onward to five continents in a day.

questions.q: How do large farms contribute to pathogen spread?
a: Manure pools breed pathogens that contaminate soil and water
They import animals from many different countries
They use antibiotics that create new viruses
They crowd workers into small dormitories
questions.why: Lesson 2 says manure pools on large farms become breeding grounds that contaminate air, soil and water.

questions.q: What did Aaron Burr do with the waterworks money?
a: Used most of it for a bank, leaving a poor water system
Spent it all on clean drinking water
Returned the money to the taxpayers
Gave it to doctors for medical research
questions.why: Lesson 3 says Burr diverted most of the waterworks money to a bank, leaving contaminated water for 50 years.

questions.q: Why was the cholera fluid treatment dismissed?
a: Doctors believed disease came from miasmas, not lost fluids
It was far too expensive for most hospitals
The treatment had dangerous side effects
No doctor knew how to administer it
questions.why: Lesson 3 says doctors dismissed fluid replacement because they believed diseases came from miasmas.
